calls.head: There’s no curse: Hofer against the Sharks
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Hofer has been shaky against the Sharks, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
calls.call: If Hofer starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .911 than to his .865 against the Sharks.

calls.said: the Blues would allow fewer dangerous shots than the Sharks
calls.beyond: St. Louis usually gets better looks than most teams, and San Jose usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 10.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 6.9% against San Jose) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis a 63% chance, but San Jose had other ideas.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 37% chance, and they proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Sharks shake off a slow start
paras: Connor McMichael struck first for the Blues early in the first, but Tyler Toffoli made it 1-1 for San Jose midway through the second. Dillon Dubé scored his first goal for St. Louis shorthanded early in the third to put the Blues ahead 2-1. Collin Graf tied it 2-2 for San Jose four and a half minutes later. Darnell Nurse scored his first goal for San Jose just over a minute into overtime to win it.

The Blues had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Blues win about six in ten. Alex Nedeljkovic was the difference, stopping 24 of 26. The Sharks had three shots in the first period and trailed 1-0, then outshot the Blues 24-15 the rest of the way. Joel Hofer stopped 24 of 27 for the Blues.
The Blues hit two posts and still lost. The Sharks improved to 3-1-0, and the Blues fell to 1-2-1 in their home opener.
